items.bodyText: Francis Howell Families They are, but you’re presenting this as though they are mutually exclusive. Tech integration is indispensable in the modern classroom. Teachers still teach. There is no replacement for good teaching. I haven’t seen anybody push for this to replace teaching. It’s rare to find high quality, research supported resources without a tech component in 2026. Laptops and technology are not going away. Additionally, if we can level the playing field for kids by giving them equal access without additional costs, that’s an example of equity being a good thing.

items.author: Michael Kern
items.bodyText: I don't like to Post on Social Media, but my heart felt prayers for all parties. Politics is ugly. It was ugly when I ran and won in the 80's and it is even uglier now with Social Media. I hope that children aren't harmed by the results. It is one thing to run, but the "heavy lifting" starts after the results are in. You need a certain skill set to do this. Deal with all types of people that you percieve as being "crazy" but yet handle the situation. I am not referring to any of the candidates, but myself. As a retired IT professional I live best in the black & white. Humans and human situations live in the "gray". You need a profound sense of situational awareness to survive in this space.

items.author: Melinda Tarter
items.bodyText: Jerry Reich Jr MY kids have been raised to talk to us about ANYTHING and we talk to them about topics on the news, world issues, political, religious and sexual. I CAN and DO talk with our kids.My kids have also been taught to respect others and manners and that is part of the reason they started hating going to public school because of the kids who ran wild and caused all of the tantrums and disruptions and took away from them learning in a calm environment.So we did what was right for our family and removed them from the situation and to a better learning environment where they have thrived and actually learned more on a daily basis without all of the behavior issues tgst never get addressed and fixed in public school.I volunteered at their school 3 days a week from anywhere to 1-3 hours daily, so I saw all of the stuff that went on ! I also had lunch regularly with my kids and enjoyed talking with their friends; however it wasn’t long before lunchtime was so loud with all of the talking and hollering and yelling you had to scream to the people sitting next to you to hear them and carry on a conversation. We tried calling their dad during lunch one day so they could talk to him and they couldn’t even talk because of all the noise. That was another huge reason to pull them from public schools.My husband and I were both raised to talk to our parents about anything and to come to them with any problem no matter how big or small we thought they were and we would work it out. That also meant to call home no matter what time and no questions would be asked , just so we were safe. THAT IS WHAT WE HAVE INSTILLED IN IUR KIDS.It’s great for kids to be able to confide in their teacher and havr a good relationship; however keeping important information from the parents is not okay.The kids are minors and their parents have every right to know if something serious is going on with their kids.

items.author: Lauren Nevatt
items.bodyText: Fact- currently for secondary level chromebook carts are in each classroom. Those carts are stocked to have enough chromebooks for the highest attendance the class could have. In education, you don't consistently have the same amount of students for every section. Therefore in these carts you would have more items then student population. **Going 1 to 1 allows you to only purchase the amount of technology you'd actually need for student population. Therefore the technology budget could be smaller or able to purchase other technology needs. (Please consider how often the average person changes their cellphone, TV, etc. Sorry technology is just always changing/aging-these cycles are out of our circle of control we don't develop technology in education and educators are told from the state level platforms that are approved to determine students academic understanding) -if you would prefer paper testing like we did "back in my day" I would suggest talking to our law makers in Jeff City.Another fact I have learned from being in a 1 to 1 district-students learn responsibility. They have to understand, just as an adult how to keep your technology safe. Most adults travel with their work computer and have to know how to keep it safe. We will build that within our students now too. Fact all state testing- MAP, EOC, dyslexia reading tests are all on digital platforms only. These all have windows for how quickly they need to be completed by, so data can be reviewed and shared to state and parents as well as used to change instruction for students.Fact- most jobs utilize technology and the job force expects employees to come out with basic understandings of how programs work.If you want to vote for the people in the article sure go ahead, but the beginning part of your article needed more facts for voters to understand context of why technology is in our districts.

items.bodyText: We do prioritize academics, our library (at elementary level anyway) is definitely age appropriate, and we have full/time officers in every school. Spend some time with us—spend some time with the kids.

items.author: Christopher Brooks
items.bodyText: Mica Veihman you seem to have a fundamental misunderstanding about the purpose and procedures behind sunshine requests. You also seem to be misinformed that this is new or unusual. I suggest you talk to your friends in Francis Howell Forward about all the emails they have sunshined over the years, and all the student data that the SCCFPS PAC and the teachers union have sunshined as well. Your outrage is both manufactured and misplaced. Just to debunk one of your incorrect claims - no one reads through every email. An IT staffer does a search on the server for the specified keywords, and that returns a list of matching emails. Then the custodian of records in the district, whose job it is to look at things like this, surveys the emails and redacts personal information. There are many exceptions in the law that allow for privacy protections and make sure that personal non-relevant information is excluded. The staffers doing this work in the districts are very sensitive to the improper release of information.

items.author: Linda Reeves
items.bodyText: I've contacted my legislators. Thank you for making it easier to do so by providing their contact information. I absolutely support SB 1002 to move St. Charles County school board elections and tax issues to the November. Historically, April elections have proven low voter turn out which is not representative of the majority of the people. All elections are important and should take place when the most people vote. I have no suggestions as to how to increase vote participation in April, but perhaps a better strategy would be to just simply move them to November versus fighting a battle to get people to the polls in April. Thank you for everything you do!

items.author: Jason Henke
items.bodyText: Disclaimer:These are my opinions and do not reflect the opinions of any Board member(s) and/or Staff of the Wentzville School District. Over here in the WSD shortly after Renee first got on the Board she started asking questions about all of the wasted spending. Such as a $300 toy high chair from Amazon. She quickly found out the previous Superintendent did not like questions being asked of her or her staff. She claimed that Renee was creating a "hostile" work environment! The previous Superintendent, previous board leadership, inside counsel, and outside counsel also "called" that "Harassment", "Retaliation", "Intimidation", with a sprinkle of "Micromanaging".Simply asking questions as a Board member landed her some complaints from the previous Superintendent, which to this day...she's "not allowed" to see, or have a copy of; per inside counsel and outside counsel. Cute huh! Inside counsel working with his boss and outside counsel to help weaponize Board policy against Board members she didn't like. Who's working for who here??? Total conflict of interest. In the end, the previous Superintendent, previous board leadership, inside counsel, and outside counsel decided to investigate Renee, Jen, and David and PARENTS (Which some of them included Renee and Jen's Treasurer) all behind closed doors using Our Tax dollars costing the Tax Payers around a half a million dollars. For what?!?! All for nothing. Nothing happened.In the end the previous Superintendent used the other half of the previous board and her inside counsel along with 4 to 5 outside law firms to get a 1.2 million dollar pay out.I believe this was a total inside job. I believe it was Corruption, Collusion, Intimidating Elected Officials, Misuse of Tax Payer Funds, Oaths of Office, Disenfranchised Voters, etc... Investigating PARENTS without their knowledge using Tax Payer Funds is against USC 1983.This was bad. All bad, and was all started by a motion Julie Scott made, and is now running for re-election.

items.author: Larry Blandino
items.bodyText: Carissa Rhoads Figgins Since you help with those kids who have a disability, I admire the heck out of you. Blessings to you. DEI is very different than IDEA. I support IDEA, not DEI. DEI is simply an amorphous and ultimately, autocratic concept that can be anything one on the Left wants it to be to promote what many parents consider to be a harmful education agenda. It should be noted that being female or black or gender confused are NOT examples of disabilities covered by IDEA.In short, the Individuals with Disabilities Education Acts is a LAW that strives to provide free and appropriate education, and assure specific and measurable goals in the least restrictive educational environment. Many students with disabilities include those with autism, Down Syndrome, behavior issues, and other health impairments.

items.bodyText: Francis Howell Families You are correct, only sitting on a computer is not a great source of learning. How many courses are 100% driven by technology in Francis Howell without teacher instruction? I don't believe we have any, however I am open to any facts you have on that. Students however do need to understand how to get some instruction from technology because in the workforce not all training is provided via human to human. It is a job of an educator to prepare a student to understand how to learn with and from the tools technology platforms provide.Please don't try to tell me, an educator and a parent who receives all of the physical paper assignments that my children bring home, that our educators are only relying on technology only to educate our youth. Also, to your statement I never said anything in regards to which teaching style was better, please do not put words in my mouth that I simply never shared.You are welcome to your opinion, but I just wanted to point out facts you had missed in your article. While perhaps your article was meant to not have all of the details regarding the district and the ways in which it makes choices, I felt it was my duty as a member of this page and this community to let others know more facts regarding the topic, as it related to the district and technology. Thank you, for allowing me to share my opinion on your public post, I hope you have a relaxing weekend and find time to enjoy the beautiful weather.

items.author: Henry Kriss
items.bodyText: The receipts are in. If you are a teacher who has ever written a dues check and assumed it was going toward better pay, stronger benefits, or a decent contract, read carefully. A new report from Defending Education has blown the lid off one of the most brazen political money machines in American history, and your money is in it.Since August 2015, the National Education Association (NEA) and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) have funneled a combined $669,324,912.33 in member dues and PAC funds into left-wing political entities, far-left nonprofits, and Democratic campaigns. Fold in state and local affiliates, and the total surpasses $1 billion.The big money tells the story. The State Engagement Fund, a Democratic Party infrastructure vehicle, received $60,525,000. The For Our Future Action Fund took $44,732,078. The Senate Majority PAC received $32,655,000. The House Majority PAC got $25,842,790. The Strategic Victory Fund, created in 2020 explicitly to defeat Donald Trump, received $19,300,000.On top of all that, the unions pumped over $85 million directly into Democrat Party entities at every level of government, not counting a single dollar in individual candidate contributions. The Biden Victory Fund received $923,500. The Hillary Victory Fund got $444,250. The Bill, Hillary, and Chelsea Clinton Foundation collected $725,000, with another $400,000 to the Clinton Global Initiative.https://redstate.com/ben-smith/2026/04/29/teachers-dues-became-a-1b-democrat-slush-fundnot-classroom-funding-n2201843

items.author: Francis Howell Families
items.bodyText: Laurie Ann Amending a report is not the same as committing an ethics violation and it is important to extensively research MEC rules prior to running for office. Amending a report can be done for multiple reasons without committing any violation but funding a Political Action Committee with your campaign funds is a MEC violation. Oelke’s MEC report directly states she paid $400 to a PAC, it will be up to the MEC to determine what to do about this.
